fixes.explanation: God says, "…I gave her a certificate of divorce and sent her away." (Jeremiah 3:8) It happened because faithless Israel had committed adultery. That's the paper in this verse.

God says, "I will no longer look on you with anger, for I am merciful…" (Jeremiah 3:12) That's God's own reason, right there in His words. And He adds, "I will not be angry forever." Say that one out loud, baker.

God says, "Only acknowledge your guilt, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God." (Jeremiah 3:13) Notice that word "only." No receipt, no apology tour, just own it. Easier said than done, I know.
God says of that time, "They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts." (Jeremiah 3:17) That's part of what He says about that time. It's a promise for the days ahead.
God says, "If you will remove your detestable idols from My sight and no longer waver…" (Jeremiah 4:1) That's what He names to remove from His sight. And it begins with an "if," so it's an open door.

God says, "…then the nations will be blessed by Him, and in Him they will glory." (Jeremiah 4:2) The blessing reaches the nations, not just Israel. That's a big blessing hanging on a small word like "if."

I'd love for that to be so, but it's not what God says. He says, "…My wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it, because of your evil deeds." (Jeremiah 4:4) Nothing there says it flares for a moment and then passes. This one is heavy, so the answer is False.

Right. God says, "Otherwise, My wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it, because of your evil deeds." (Jeremiah 4:4) Nothing in that says it flares for a moment and passes. I think it's a heavy verse, and it's a good reason to listen to that word return.
